title: Brown gives the right adjoint of proper localizing pushforward
statement:
Fix a universe u, a prime $\ell$, and a field $k$ in universe u of positive
characteristic different from $\ell$. Let $Z,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes
and let $g:Z\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be
a commutative condensed ring with its specified multiplication and a certificate
of one of the three adic coefficient families [def-sfb-adic-coefficient-certificate].
For $T=Z,Y$, put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$, let $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$
be the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category
[sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], let $\mathcal B_T$ be its bounded constructible
full subcategory [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and let
$\mathcal L_T=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal B_T)$ be the full localizing hull, using
ambient coproducts indexed in universe u+1
[def-sfb-bounded-constructible-localizing-closure].
Let $F_g:\mathcal L_Z\to\mathcal L_Y$ be the actual localizing restriction of
$Rg_*$ [lem-sfb-adic-proper-localizing-pushforward]. Then $F_g$ has a right
adjoint. More explicitly, for every $K\in\mathcal L_Y$ the functor
$M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F_gM,K)$ is representable on $\mathcal L_Z$.

source.place: Part (2): apply Brown on the localizing categories, before geometric restriction.

proof.text: For K form the additive functor H=F_g.op followed by the additive Yoneda functor of K. Opposite exactness and the cohomological Yoneda theorem make H cohomological. Since F_g preserves coproducts, F_g.op preserves the corresponding products; Yoneda preserves products. Reflect the latter preservation along the faithful additive-group forgetful functor.
Apply cohomological Brown on the source hull to represent H. Its underlying functor is definitionally F_g.op followed by Yoneda(K).

These representations make rightAdjointObjIsDefined equal top. Apply Functor.isLeftAdjoint_of_rightAdjointObjIsDefined_eq_top. Universal representing bijections assemble the right adjoint functor, uniquely up to compatible isomorphism.
